packages.label: אֱמוּנָה וּפְנִימִיּוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ
packages.label_en: Faith and the Inwardness of the Soul
packages.reason: The entire teaching of Torah #173 revolves around one central identification: the root of faith (שרש האמונה), the inwardness of faith (פנימיות האמונה), and the inwardness of the soul (פנימיות הנפש) are declared to be one and the same reality — 'הַנֶּפֶשׁ וְהָאֱמוּנָה הֵם בְּחִינָה אַחַת'. These three nodes form a tight bechina chain (edges 2503 and 2504). The כ' letter (אות כ"ף) enters this cluster because the Rebbe states it 'hints at the bechina of Shekhinah Pnimiyut' (line 4) and the Etz Chaim confirms 'הַכֶּתֶר הִיא פְּנִימִיּוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ' while 'הַכ' הִיא בְּחִינַת כֶּתֶר' (line 5, edge 1529). Thus כתר is a bechina of פנימיות הנפש by transitivity confirmed in the same text, and אות כ"ף is a bechina of כתר. All five nodes share the same essential nature: the hidden, innermost dimension of the soul and faith, which writing (כתב) both expresses and reveals to the true tzaddik. This is a wholly positive/good domain — it concerns the innermost holiness of the Jewish soul.
